# Fixtures: ground truth for every reader

`out/` holds one image per format OmniTrace reads plus a `<name>.expected.yaml`
that says exactly what is inside it. Everything is generated by `generate.py`
from the same file tree with pinned timestamps and content, so two builds are
byte-identical and a reader is tested against facts, never against another
tool's output. The long-form description (the tree, the per-format history
semantics, the YAML schema, determinism) is in
[docs/TESTING.md](../../docs/TESTING.md); this file is the map of the
directory and of the two checkers that consume it.

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `generate.py` | Builds every image and writes `out/<name>.expected.yaml` and `out/index.yaml`. `--only NAME`, `--skip-missing`, `-v`. Needs PyYAML and the mkfs tools. |
| `build.sh` | Runs `generate.py` inside the Docker image (`Dockerfile`) so every tool is present; `--native` uses the host tools; `--check` builds twice and compares. `scripts/fixtures.sh` wraps it. |
| `Dockerfile` | debian:bookworm with squashfs-tools, mtd-utils, e2fsprogs, dosfstools, mtools and yaffs2utils. |
| `check_listing.py` | Compares an OmniTrace `listing.yaml` (or a directory of `analyze` cases) with the ground truth. See below. |
| `out/` | Generated. Regenerate, never edit. |

## What a fixture guarantees

`<name>.expected.yaml` (`schema: omnitrace-fixture/1`) carries:

- `image`: file name, format id (the same id the signature/validator and the
  reader registry use: `squashfs`, `jffs2`, `ext4`, `fat32`, ...), size,
  sha256, the tool and argv that built it.
- `features`: what the format can represent (`symlink`, `hardlink`, `mode`,
  `owner`, `mtime_resolution`). A check that the format cannot express is not
  made: FAT has no modes or owners and keeps even seconds.
- `tree`: the live tree after the history script ran, sorted by path, one
  entry per file with kind, mode (octal string), uid, gid, size, sha256
  (regular files), `link_target` (symlinks), `hardlink_of` + `nlink` (hard
  links) and mtime.
- `history` (fixtures with a scripted overwrite/delete): `superseded` (older
  versions still on the medium: path, inode, version, size, sha256, mtime),
  `current`, `deleted` (files with no live directory entry), and format
  notes; `content_recoverable: false` marks a version whose bytes may have
  been reused.
- `attrs`: format specifics a reader's `info()` should agree with.

Wrapper fixtures (`mbr-two-partitions`, `gpt`, `ubi`, `nested`,
`uimage-lzma`) have `partitions:` / `volumes:` / `layers:` / `payload:`
instead of a tree and name the inner fixture whose YAML describes the
contents.

## Who checks against it

**`test_filesystems` (C++, automatic).**
`tests/unit/filesystems/fixture_conformance_test.cpp` instantiates one
parameter per `out/*.expected.yaml` and, for every fixture whose format has a
reader in `fs::FilesystemRegistry`, runs four checks (live tree, history,
DiskSink extraction, determinism). Fixtures without a reader are skipped with
a message naming the format, and `FixtureCoverage.Report` prints the whole
table. Nothing is registered per reader: a new reader is covered the moment
its `OMNITRACE_REGISTER_FILESYSTEM` line exists. The YAML is read by
`fixture_yaml.{h,cpp}`, a dependency-free parser for the subset PyYAML
writes. Details and the contract a reader has to meet:
[docs/TESTING.md, section 3](../../docs/TESTING.md#3-conformance-harness).

```sh
./build/linux-gcc/src/filesystems/test_filesystems --gtest_filter='Fixture*'
./build/linux-gcc/src/filesystems/test_filesystems --gtest_filter='*FixtureConformance*/jffs2_history'
```

**`check_listing.py` (Python, for case directories).** The same comparison
applied to what the CLI wrote, so an examiner or CI can verify a case
without the test binary.

```sh
# One filesystem: the listing the CLI wrote against the ground truth.
omnitrace analyze tests/fixtures/out/jffs2-history.img --out /tmp/c --history
tests/fixtures/check_listing.py tests/fixtures/out/jffs2-history.expected.yaml \
    /tmp/c/filesystems/n000002/listing.yaml --history

# A directory of cases, one per fixture, with a PASS/FAIL/SKIP line each.
for img in tests/fixtures/out/*.img; do
  n=$(basename "$img" .img)
  omnitrace analyze "$img" --out /tmp/cases/"$n" --history
done
tests/fixtures/check_listing.py --cases /tmp/cases --history
```

- Without `--history` the live tree is checked: every `tree` entry present
  with matching kind, mode, owner, size, link target, mtime (within the
  format's resolution), nlink and sha256; hard-linked pairs share an inode;
  no extra live paths (except `lost+found` on ext). Entries flagged
  `deleted` or `superseded` in the listing are ignored, so a listing made
  with `--history` still passes.
- With `--history` the `history` section is checked as well: every
  `superseded` entry must be in the listing with `superseded: true` and the
  same `version`, every `deleted` entry with `deleted: true` (under its path
  or, when the name could not be recovered, `lost+found/<inode>`), each with
  matching size, inode, mtime and sha256 (unless `content_recoverable:
  false`).
- `--cases DIR` walks `DIR/<fixture-name>/` (or `DIR` itself when it is one
  case; the name then comes from the manifest's evidence file), finds
  `filesystems/*/listing.yaml`, and for MBR/GPT fixtures checks each
  partition's listing (matched by the filesystem node's offset in `INFO.yaml`)
  against the inner fixture. Exit 1 when any fixture fails; `--fixtures DIR`
  points at a different `out/`.

## Adding a fixture

`docs/EXTENDING.md`, "Add a fixture image": a `build_<name>()` in
`generate.py`, a row in `BUILDERS`, the tool in the Dockerfile, then
`scripts/fixtures.sh build && scripts/fixtures.sh check`. The conformance
test picks the new `expected.yaml` up on the next run.
